claim: Milestone 2A frozen efficiency protocol: artifact size, single-thread CPU latency and throughput, and process memory for V1-V4 on one machine. Outcomes are reported as measured with their spread; no speed or memory claim is assumed. Pilot results are non-scientific development checks (1 seed, 2 epochs, small subsets, validation data only) and carry no accuracy or robustness conclusion.

threads.secondary_scope: campaign: run with 4 threads as a second pass

fixed_inputs.rule: np.random.default_rng(derived_seed('efficiency-rows', split_seed)).choice without replacement from the supplied validation rows, sorted by position; IDs and a hash of the scaled rows are saved

schedule: interleaved: repetition 1 runs V1, V2, V3, V4, repetition 2 runs V1, V2, V3, V4, and so on; retried processes are appended at the end and flagged; the executed order is never re-sorted
timed_region: input row tensor -> repeat to 50 positions -> model forward -> argmax
excluded_from_timing: CSV reading, MinMax scaling (a fixed affine operation identical for all models), attack generation, calibration, model loading, process start-up

memory.baseline: process RSS after imports and model/checkpoint load, before the first inference
memory.peak: Linux VmHWM from /proc/self/status (peak resident set, process lifetime) after the timed runs; Windows peak_wset is used only on Windows. Windows pilot (peak working set) and Linux (VmHWM) memory numbers are not comparable
memory.cross_check: provenance.MemoryMonitor with a 10 ms sampling interval, run in a separate untimed pass after the timed runs so that the sampling thread does not disturb latency
memory.caveat: process-wide RSS is coarse and includes allocator slack and the imported Python packages (identical for every variant)

artifact_size: bytes of torch.save(model.state_dict()); no optimizer, calibration tensors or logs
